title: Pork Carnitas
subtitle: Slow-roasted pulled pork with crispy edges
excerpt: Carnitas means little meats in Spanish. Pork shoulder cooks low and slow until it can be shredded with a fork, then goes back under high heat to get crisped edges. Serve piled into warm tortillas with avocado and salsa.
sourceNotes: Carnitas is a classic of Michoacan, Mexico, traditionally cooked by confiting pork slowly in lard in copper pots. The oven method produces similar results more accessibly and is now the standard home approach.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the shredded pork in its juices for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen in a wide pan until hot and re-crisp the edges.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the pork up to 2 days ahead. Refrigerate, then re-crisp in a hot oven or pan before serving.

content.text: This recipe uses lime and honey in place of the traditional orange juice. The acidity and sweetness perform the same role, helping the pork brown and adding a fruity background note. If you have an orange, use the juice of one instead.
Heat the oven to 160 C. Mix the cumin, oregano, smoked paprika, garlic, lime juice, honey and olive oil with 1 teaspoon of salt to make a paste.
Toss the pork chunks in the paste to coat. Transfer to a roasting tin along with the onion. Add 200ml of water.
Cover tightly with foil and roast for 2.5 to 3 hours until the pork is very tender and pulls apart easily.
Remove the foil. Shred the pork roughly with two forks directly in the tin. Spread it out in an even layer.
Increase the oven to 220 C and return the tin for 15 to 20 minutes until the edges of the pork are crispy and caramelised.
Serve in warm tortillas with avocado, salsa and lime wedges.

items.symptom: Pork is still tough after 3 hours.
items.cause: The oven was too hot and the liquid evaporated too fast.
items.fix: Add 100ml more water and cook for another 30 minutes covered.

items.symptom: Edges are not crisping in the final stage.
items.cause: Too much liquid remains in the tin.
items.fix: Spoon off excess liquid before turning the oven up.
